Avery,

We're seeing intermittent egress silence from our on-prem cluster to external services immediately after the HA gateway cutover this morning (cutover at 07:58 PDT). Client requests to external APIs show SYNs leaving our hosts but no responses for up to 20s before TCP retransmit fires and things recover sporadically. This is affecting our production webhooks and a batch job.

What we observed so far:
- Cutover completed at 07:58 (our side).
- TCP flows show initial SYN -> no SYN/ACK for ~15-20s, then recovery.
- Traceroutes show a different next-hop after failover (edge egress IP changed).
- We also see fragmented packet warnings in the app logs right after the cutover window.

Attached a short capture snippet (capture-snippet.txt) with timestamps and a small tcpdump excerpt. We can share a full pcap if that helps.

This is high priority for us — can we get immediate help? Who should we loop in from your side?

Thanks,
Craig Turner

Craig — thanks for the quick heads up and the snippet. Sorry you're hitting this. I'm looping in Laura (networking lead) and Markus (operations) to triage immediately.

Quick asks while we start digging:
- Please share the full pcap for the 07:50–08:10 window if you can (pcap preferred).
- Paste a short traceroute from one of the affected hosts and the gateway (traceroute -n -w 2 8.8.8.8).
- Confirm whether the on-prem edge interfaces were switched to jumbo frames (9000 MTU) as part of the cutover.
- Any changes to NAT pools / SNAT ranges during the cutover?

Based on experience, this pattern can be caused by a combination of: asymmetric return path after failover, security group/conntrack state invalidation when source IPs change, or MTU-induced fragmentation causing drops at a middlebox. We will triage in that order and propose a short mitigation playbook (MSS clamp on gateway + pin NAT to old source IP + extend conntrack timeout) while we investigate root cause.

ETA from our side for initial remediation steps: 30–45 minutes. I will coordinate with you for a canary first.

> Avery,

Thanks Craig — good details. A few things I want to call out and requests for targeted artifacts so we can prioritize steps: 

Suspected causes (initial):
- Asymmetric return path / new egress IP: if the gateway NAT pool moved and return packets are coming back a different path, conntrack on the application side or a stateful SG can drop replies for the established tuple.
- MTU mismatch / jumbo frames: if hosts went to 9000 MTU but the carrier/edge path is 1500, you'll see fragmented frames or DF drops; some devices drop fragments or don't forward large packets when DF is set.
- Conntrack table churn: a large number of simultaneous flows during the failover can evict state entries.

Can you provide (preferably pasted inline or in the pcap):
1) The tcpdump lines showing the initial SYN and any ICMP 'fragmentation needed' or RSTs.
2) The gateway ARP/NAT translation snapshot right after cutover (nat table dump / iptables -t nat -L -n or your vendor equivalent).
3) If possible, a router-level interface MTU show for the path (we just need to confirm mismatch).

Immediate mitigations we can apply from your side (low-risk canary):
- MSS clamping on the egress gateway to 1436 (to avoid fragmentation). Command (example): iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
- If NAT pool changed, temporarily pin the problematic internal host to the previous public IP (static SNAT) for a short window (we can give exact commands once you share NAT details).
- Increase conntrack timeout for established TCP on the gateway for 5–10m to avoid immediate eviction during the window.

I'll stand by for the pcap/traceroute and will start a quick lab repro for asymmetric return path + SG state to confirm expected behavior and capture evidence for the postmortem.

Laura
Senior Network Engineer — Redwood Inference

What we captured:
- Cutover at 07:58:04 — immediately after that we see SYNs leaving on 10.4.2.33:40012 -> 3.7.99.45:443, but no SYN/ACK for ~18s. Then a SYN/ACK shows up and the three-way handshake completes.
- Traceroute from host A shows next-hop changed from 192.168.10.1 -> 192.168.20.1 after the cutover.
- Our gateway interface was configured for MTU 9000 earlier this morning as part of a throughput tuning patch. We didn't change that at cutover but the carrier path is 1500. That explains the fragment warnings in the app.

We did not change the NAT pool at cutover — but the gateway failover did change the source IP observed by upstream (NAT device altered ephemeral port mapping).

Attaching pcap now. Please advise the safest next steps; we can take a 5–10 minute maintenance window if needed.

Subject: Internal: remediation plan for Halcyon — MSS clamp + NAT pinning + conntrack extension (JIRA-9843)

Laura / Markus — summary and action items for the playbook (per Halcyon capture and traceroute):

Root cause hypothesis:
- Gateway HA handoff changed egress path (asymmetric return path) and the egress device was running jumbo (9000 MTU). Large packets with DF set were hitting a 1500 MTU region, causing fragments/drops. Concurrently, ephemeral NAT mapping differences caused the upstream to see different tuple -> state invalidation on some middleboxes / SGs.

Immediate canary remediation (apply one at a time, test, rollback if regressions):
1) MSS clamp at the egress gateway to 1436 (low-impact, can be added to mangle POSTROUTING).
2) Temporarily pin the most affected host(s) to previous public SNAT (static SNAT entry) for 10 minutes to validate return-path consistency.
3) Increase conntrack established timeout to 600s during the window to avoid immediate eviction.
4) If MSS clamp + conntrack extension relieve the symptom, schedule a follow-up change to standardize MTU across on-prem edge and carrier (remove jumbo where not end-to-end).

Operational notes:
- ETA to implement MSS clamp on Halcyon's gateway: 10–15 minutes (need their maintenance window).
- We'll coordinate with Craig for canary host(s) and verify recovery metrics (successful 3-way handshake latency, webhook retries).
- I'll open JIRA-9843 (link in thread) and a shared Drive doc for the postmortem/standards update: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-HaHandoff-Postmortem

Markus — can you draft the exact iptables/tunnel commands and a rollback snippet? Once you have that, I'll coordinate the maintenance window with Craig. Laura — can you run a quick lab with asymmetric return + SG state to confirm expected behavior and capture evidence for the postmortem?

Thanks both — aim to have the canary applied within the next 2 hours.
